headline: Granted variances for properties at 42 Giles Street, 1135 Paradise Avenue, and 20 Woodbine Street.
summary: Variance requests were heard for properties on Giles Street, Paradise Avenue, and Woodbine Street. All three variances were granted. Minutes from the May 21, 2026 meeting were also approved.
decisions: Granted side and front yard setback variances at 42 Giles Street, with all members voting in favor.
Granted a variance for a subdivision at 1135 Paradise Avenue, with all members in favor.
Granted lot coverage and side yard setback variances at 20 Woodbine Street, with all members in favor.
Approved the May 21, 2026 meeting minutes as written, 4-0, with Commissioner Walsh abstaining.

September 10, 2026 Zoning Board of Appeals 
 Meeting Minutes 
   
The Hamden Zoning Board of Appeals  held a hybrid Public Hearing and Special Meeting on 
Thursday, September 3, 2026 at 7:00pm. The meeting was held in -person at Hamden Government 
Center (2750 Dixwell Avenue, Hamden, CT 06518), but was moved from the 3rd Floor Conference Room 
to the Parks and Recreation Department Conference Room , and remotely via Town Zoom 
teleconferencing software at https://hamden.zoom.us/j/82445626188. 
 
Commissioners in Attendance: In-Person: Paul Fioretti (Chair), Nancy Saravis-Foote, John 
Brantley, Francesca Provenzano, Steve Walsh 
  
Staff in Attendance: In-Person: Eugene Livshits (Town Planner), Maisie Albis 
(Commission Clerk)  
 Via Zoom: Genevieve Bertolini (Stenographer) 
  
Chairman Fioretti called the meeting to order at 7:02p.m. Members and staff introduced 
themselves. There was a quorum, with alternate Commissioner Walsh filling a vacancy on the Board. 
 
A. Public Comment Session 
 There were no comments as there were no public attendees.   
 
B. Public Hearing 
 1. Variance #26-6737  
42 Giles Street 
Applicant: Leslie Casanova 
Variance requested from: 
(1) Section 220 Table 2.3 
i. requesting 10.875-foot side yard setback where a minimum of 12 feet is required 
ii. requesting 24.5-foot front yard setback where a minimum of 25 feet is required 
Leslie Casanova presented the application. She explained that she and her daughter are 
looking to construct a small addition to the daughter’s home. The addition would provide space
Page 2 of 5 Zoning Board of Appeals 9.3.26 Meeting Minutes 
for Ms. Casanova to live with her daughter in the home, as well as general living space and a 
one-car garage. She said that the garage would offer security and protection from the elements. 
Its footprint would extend into the side and front yard setbacks by roughly 13 inches and 6 
inches, respectively, thus necessitating the requested variance. 
Chairman Fioretti called for questions from members. Commissioner Provenzano noted that 
the location of an existing carport appeared to have already created a nonconformity on the lot. 
The Chairman confirmed, but explained that this proposal required a separate variance request 
since the garage would not be constructed within the area of the preexisting nonconformity. The 
original nonconformity will be reduced with the removal of the carport.  
There were no further questions from the Board. Chairman Fioretti called for public 
comments regarding the application; there were none. The Chairman closed the public hearing 
on the item. 
 
2. Variance #26-6738 
1135 Paradise Avenue 
Applicant: McNamara Builders & General Contractors 
Variance requested from: 
(1) Section 530.2.2(c)—requesting a subdivision comprised of 75% rear lots where a maximum 
of 15% is allowed  
Civil engineer Marcus Puttock presented the application. He was joined by property owner 
Steve McNamara. Mr. Puttock first described the lot, explaining that the nearly 11-acre parcel 
was irregularly shaped with very narrow street frontage. He said that even a simple split would 
result in nonconformity as one of the two (50%) would be a rear lot. 
Mr. Puttock reported that the applicant had explored other possibilities, such as the 
possibility of splitting the parcel into as many as eleven new lots and constructing a new road for 
access. It was determined through the design process that the current proposal would be 
significantly less disruptive in its construction and more fitting for the neighborhood overall.  
The subdivision as submitted would include a large open space at the rear of the property, 
one lot with frontage on Paradise Avenue, and three interior lots requiring access ways from the 
street. Mr. Puttock noted the similarities of the proposed access ways to those of several adjacent 
parcels. The hardship, he said, stems from the irregular shape of the parcel. It does not allow for 
a typical subdivision without a major reconfiguration of the area; Mr. Puttock assessed that the 
current proposal is a better use of the land and more appropriate with consideration to the health 
and safety of the neighborhood. 
Mr. Livshits prompted Mr. Puttock to clarify the changes made to the plan since its original 
submission. Mr. Puttock highlighted the access way to Lot #4, which had been shortened. He 
explained that the original dimension exceeded the maximum 400-foot length allowed by the 
subdivision and zoning regulations.
Page 3 of 5 Zoning Board of Appeals 9.3.26 Meeting Minutes 
In response to a question from Commissioner Provenzano, Mr. Puttock said that length of the 
access way was reduced by making Lot #3 a bit smaller and bringing Lot #4 slightly closer to the 
road. Commissioner Walsh asked about the access way to Lot #2. Mr. Puttock confirmed that Lot 
#2 had its own access way adjacent and parallel to that of Lot #4. Chairman Fioretti inquired 
whether there were other subdivisions in Hamden with similar access roads. Mr. Puttock pointed 
to the adjacent parcels he had noted previously. The Chairman then asked if the open space 
depicted on the plan was part of the applicant’s property. Mr. Puttock confirmed, adding that it is 
undevelopable without road access from the east of the property.  
There were no further questions from members. Chairman Fioretti called for public 
comments, and there were none. He then closed the public hearing for the item. 
 
3. Variance #26-6739 
20 Woodbine Street 
Applicant: Stephanie Dunson & Amy Cheng 
Variance requested from: 
(1) Section 220 Table 2.1—requesting lot coverage of 25.2% where a maximum of 25% is 
allowed 
(2) Section 220 Table 2.3—requesting 11.8-foot side yard setback where a minimum of 12 feet 
is required  
Attorney Joseph Porto presented the application, accompanied by project designer Annie 
Jaroszewicz. He stated that the applicants are seeking to construct an addition to their home. The 
addition would be designed to ADA standards to accommodate a family member with 
disabilities, he said. The existing home is on an undersized 0.14-acre lot in the R4 zone, which 
Mr. Porto cited as the cause of the hardship. Mr. Porto then reviewed a site plan to show the 
existing and proposed conditions.  
Commissioner Brantley noted that the application form indicated use of both septic and 
public sewer systems and asked for clarification. Mr. Porto believed that to be a mistake and said 
that the site had public water and sewer services.  
Commissioner Saravis-Foote asked whether the applicant had heard from neighbors 
regarding their thoughts on the proposal. Mr. Porto referenced a letter in support that had been 
submitted with the application and said he had not heard of any objections. Ms. Jaroszewicz 
added that the applicants had circulated the plans to neighbors who had expressed their support. 
Chairman Fioretti raised mild concerns about the removal of the existing driveway given that 
parking bans are frequent in the winters; he advised that the applicants keep that in mind.  
There were no further questions from members. The Chairman called for comments from the 
public, and there were none. He closed the public hearing for the item.
Page 4 of 5 Zoning Board of Appeals 9.3.26 Meeting Minutes 
C. Regular Meeting 
 1. Variance #26-6737  
42 Giles Street 
Applicant: Leslie Casanova 
Variance requested from: 
(1) Section 220 Table 2.3 
iii. requesting 10.875-foot side yard setback where a minimum of 12 feet is required 
iv. requesting 24.5-foot front yard setback where a minimum of 25 feet is required 
Commissioner Brantley moved to approve the variance request as submitted, seconded 
by Commissioner Provenzano. Chairman Fioretti remarked that the applicant had done their 
best to design in accordance with the regulations and was requesting only modest relief. With no 
further discussion, he called for a vote. All members voted in favor and the requested 
variance was granted.  
 
2. Variance #26-6738 
1135 Paradise Avenue 
Applicant: McNamara Builders & General Contractors 
Variance requested from: 
(1) Section 530.2.2(c)—requesting a subdivision comprised of 75% rear lots where a maximum 
of 15% is allowed 
Commissioner Saravis-Foote moved to approve the variance request as submitted. 
Commissioner Brantley seconded and all were in favor. The requested variance was 
granted unanimously.  
 
3. Variance #26-6739 
20 Woodbine Street 
Applicant: Stephanie Dunson & Amy Cheng 
Variance requested from: 
(1) Section 220 Table 2.1—requesting lot coverage of 25.2% where a maximum of 25% is 
allowed 
(2) Section 220 Table 2.3—requesting 11.8-foot side yard setback where a minimum of 12 feet 
is required 
Commissioner Provenzano moved to approve the variance request as submitted. 
Commissioner Walsh seconded the motion. He noted that the request was minimal and that the 
ADA-compliant addition would allow the residents to accommodate a family member’s
Page 5 of 5 Zoning Board of Appeals 9.3.26 Meeting Minutes 
disabilities in their home. All members voted in favor and the requested variance was 
granted.  
 
D. Old Business 
 1. Review May 21, 2026, Public Hearing and Regular Meeting minutes 
Chairman Fioretti reviewed which members had been present in May. He called for any 
necessary corrections to the minutes. Commissioner Brantley moved to approve the May 21, 
2026, meeting minutes as written, seconded by Commissioner Provenzano. Chairman 
Fioretti and Commissioners Brantley, Provenzano, and Saravis-Foote voted in favor. 
Commissioner Walsh had not been present and thus abstained. The minutes were approved 
as written. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
E. New Business 
 No new business was introduced. 
 
F. Adjournment 
 
 
 
 
 
      
 
Commissioner Provenzano moved to adjourn. Commissioner Brantley seconded, and all 
were in favor. Chairman Fioretti adjourned the meeting at 7:41p.m.
